newsitem.title: FRANCE: French sect disbands amid deaths probe.
newsitem.headline: French sect disbands amid deaths probe.

text.p: The Horus sect based in southern France said on Saturday it was disbanding after a magistrate opened a probe into the deaths of two of its members for apparent lack of medical care.

"In view of the accusations being made against us and of the lynching we are subjected to in the media, I havd decided to stop it all," the sect's founder, Marie-Therese Castano, told a news conference.
Justice sources said the justice probe into the sect was opened earlier this month for suspected failure to assist persons in danger after two women connected to the group died in 1994 and 1995.
The group has denied the women were members.
The Horus sect was founded in 1989 in La Coucourde, near Valence.

Earlier this week, police raided the homes in southwestern France of members of a U.S.-based sect called Tabitha's Place after a 19-month-old boy died from malnutrition and an untreated heart ailment. The child's parents were remanded in custody.
French authorities have stepped up surveillance of sects following the grisly deaths of 16 members of the Order of the Solar Temple in southeastern France in December 1995.
